sentences.text: Yinlong is a basal ceratopsian dinosaur from the Late Jurassic of China.
It is the earliest known member of this group and lived as a small, primarily bipedal herbivore.
This tiny dinosaur reached a length of 1.2 meters and weighed 10 kilograms.
Despite lacking a frill and horns, it is classified as a ceratopsian.
Its long robust hindlimbs and shorter three-fingered forelimbs suggest a bipedal lifestyle.
Seven gastroliths were preserved inside the abdominal cavity of one specimen.
The genus name Yinlong translates to hidden dragon, referencing the film Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon.
American and Chinese paleontologists including Xu Xing and Catherine Forster described and named the animal in 2006.
The first fossil was an exceptionally well-preserved skeleton found in 2004 in the Shishugou Formation of Xinjiang Province, China.
The species name downsi honors William Randall Downs III, who died the year before the fossils were discovered.
A small rostral bone on the upper jaw identifies Yinlong as a ceratopsian.
Features on the skull roof are considered unique shared traits of the group Marginocephalia, which includes both pachycephalosaurs and ceratopsians.
Skull features in Yinlong resemble those of Heterodontosauridae, supporting the hypothesis that these groups are closely related.
The animal is classified within the family Chaoyangsauridae.
Yinlong lived during the Oxfordian stage of the Late Jurassic, approximately 161.2 to 155.7 million years ago.
A hypothesis linking Heterodontosauridae and Marginocephalia was not supported by subsequent analyses of Yinlong's postcranial anatomy.
